questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the black arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The basilar membrane is a layer underlying the organ of Corti, supporting it and separating it from the scala tympani below.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the "X."

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Cranial nerve VIII, the vestibulocochlear innervates the receptors in the inner ear, the maculae, the cristae ampullares and the organ of Corti. The nerve seen here is the cochlear division of the nerve located in the modiolus of the cochlea.

alternativas.texto: Vestibular division of cranial nerve VIII

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure outlined by the oval.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The cochlear duct is the portion of the membranous labyrinth located in the cochlea. Its location is intermediary between the scala vestibuli above and the scala tympani below. The cochlear duct houses the receptor for sound, the organ of Corti.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure outlined by the rectangle.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The crista ampullaris is the ridge-shaped receptor in the ampulla of each semicircular duct. The gelatinous cupula of each crista extends across the width of the ampulla and responds to body position after angular acceleration.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the two pairs of arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The macula of the utrical is a thickening in its epithelial lining. This neuroepithelial receptor is innervated by the vestibular division of cranial nerve VIII and responds to linear acceleration.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the strucure indicated by the arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The saccule and the utricle are the components of the membranous labyrinth located in the vestibule, part of the osseous labyrinth. The receptor in the saccle, the macula, responds to linear acceleration.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure in which the "X" is located.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This semicircular canal is one of three semicircular canals that form a portion of the osseous labyrinth. Each canal houses a semicircular duct, one of which is seen at the far right of this canal.

questoes.enunciado: Increased pressure in the perilymph of the structure in which the "X" is located is relieved by a bulging of the _______.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Inward movement of the stapes in the oval window increases pressure in the perilymph of the vestibule, which is transmitted through scali vestibuli and scala tympani (indicated here) to be relieved by a bulging of the round window.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the type of neuron located in the outlined area.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT: In the adult, bipolar neurons are found in organs of special sense, such as this spiral ganglion located in the cochlea. A dendrite originates in the organ of Corti and extends to the cell body of a bipolar neuron; from there, an axon emerges to form the cochlear division of cranial nerve VIII.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The stapes, one of the middle ear ossicles, is seated in the oval window separating the middle ear cavity from the vestibule (osseous labyrinth) of the inner ear.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrow.

alternativas.feedback: The tectorial membrane rests on the hair cells of the organ of Corti. Stereocilia of the hair cells are embedded in this membrane. Deflection of hair cells creates a shearing force between the stereocilia and the tectorial membrane, initiating a neural impulse.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer at the tips of the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Stria vascularis, along with related cells in the maculae and cristae ampullares, produces endolymph. The stria vascularis, an epithelium located on the outer wall of the cochlear duct, is unique in that it is the only vascularized epitheliium in mammals.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CORRECT. The basilar membrane is a layer underlying the organ of Corti, supporting it and separating it from the scala tympani below.
